speaker: narrator
text: The picnic cloth lay across the wagon. The apple catcher was behind you, and the first missing map section rested safely beside your original piece. The moonstone, rope, and journal were packed in the explorer case. Three spaces on the map were still empty.

speaker: narrator
text: A breeze slipped through the hollow. The wagon’s pennant fluttered, and Nib’s idea grew taller than his ears.

speaker: nib
text: A sail the size of the sky!

speaker: narrator
text: Nib announced grandly.

speaker: narrator
text: He tied the picnic cloth to a light wooden mast while Lark set chocks beside the wheels. The wagon stayed parked on the broad, dry path. The cloth swelled above it like a very ambitious pillow.

speaker: lark
text: A wagon the size of a mouse,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark replied cautiously. She held the rope and watched the cloth pull sideways.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib opened the journal to the apple page. He pointed to the little word you had joined before.

speaker: nib
text: I am a sailor,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib declared hopefully.

speaker: lark
text: I’ll read the other words,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark offered warmly.

speaker: lark
text: You can read am. Slide its two sounds, or join them with me.

speaker: narrator
text: The breeze grew stronger. Grass brushed against the wagon with a soft hiss. The wheels stayed snug beside their chocks, but the enormous sail tugged toward the side of the path.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib gripped his scarf. He looked at the rope, then at Lark.

speaker: nib
text: Perhaps the sky is a little large,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib admitted doubtfully.

speaker: lark
text: We can make a smaller plan,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark replied calmly. She eased the rope until the cloth stopped pulling. Nobody climbed aboard.

speaker: narrator
text: On the journal’s empty page, Lark drew a little curving letter. It bent one way, then the other: lowercase s.

speaker: lark
text: Listen to the grass,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark invited softly.

speaker: lark
text: Let a gentle stream of air make our soft hiss. No hum, and no extra little vowel. Listen to the sound, then find its letter.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib held the page flat on the explorer case. Lark drew the curving mark once more, slowly enough to follow.

speaker: nib
text: It looks as if it knows a bend in the path,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib observed thoughtfully.

speaker: lark
text: We’ll keep it beside today’s picture,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark suggested gently.

speaker: lark
text: Curve round, then curve back. Write our new s.

speaker: narrator
text: Beside the path, a low supply shelter held a folded mat and an empty cloth sack. A shallow patch of dry sand lay nearby. Lark named both objects aloud. Mat. Sack.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib considered sitting on the mat until the wind changed its mind. Then he looked at the empty sack, the sand, and the wagon’s low frame.

speaker: nib
text: Something small could help something tall,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib murmured hopefully.

speaker: lark
text: Let’s begin with the sound,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark invited warmly.

speaker: lark
text: Mat. Sack. Which one starts with the soft hiss we just learned?

speaker: narrator
text: Lark brought the sack to a flat spot beside the wagon. She folded its top outward so the opening stayed wide. A stitched line showed how much sand it needed. The sack would rest low against the frame, with a rope loop to hold it.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib scooped a little sand into it. The base spread into a soft, sturdy shape.

speaker: nib
text: A sensible sack,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib declared approvingly.

speaker: nib
text: It knows where the ground is.

speaker: lark
text: Fill it just to the stitched line,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark encouraged gently.

speaker: lark
text: Then I’ll secure its loop. The wagon will keep waiting while we work.

speaker: narrator
text: The filled sack settled low beside the explorer case. Lark fastened its loop to the wagon’s frame. Nib folded the enormous cloth down and tied it into a small sail. Every fold made the mast look less surprised.

speaker: narrator
text: The next breeze pressed against the little triangle. Lark tested the rope. The sack stayed low. The wheels stayed level. The small sail helped without pulling the parked wagon sideways.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib studied his first enormous plan, now folded into something useful.

speaker: nib
text: Still splendid,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib decided contentedly.

speaker: nib
text: Just less sky.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark showed the two versions in the journal: the great billowing cloth, and the small folded sail beside the low sand sack.

speaker: lark
text: Which sail helped our wagon stay steady?

speaker: narrator
text: Lark asked gently.

speaker: narrator
text: With the test finished, Lark removed the chocks. Nib took the handle while Lark guided the rope. Together, they brought the wagon up the broad path. The little sail helped when the breeze followed them. When it did not, your friends simply pulled.

speaker: narrator
text: At the ridge waystation, they parked beneath the shelter and set the chocks beside the wheels again. The case was safe. The first map piece was safe. Nothing new had been added to the map.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark drew the little sail and the sand sack on your next journal page. Your new s curled beside the picture. She read the connecting words aloud, and you could join am again whenever you wanted.

speaker: nib
text: Small sail. Sensible sack. Splendid sailing,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib murmured with satisfaction.

speaker: narrator
text: A soft tapping came from beneath the roof. Nib put one paw on the little table. Its far end rose a tiny way, then settled with another tap.

speaker: nib
text: That table has an idea, too,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib whispered suspiciously.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark smiled and set the journal safely on the flat floor. The wagon was steady, the windy hollow was behind you, and the tapping table could wait for your next adventure.
